messages:
anya: quick heads-up — I hit a weird interaction between shard fallback, token-throttling, and preemption during a burst test.
anya: repro steps + short log below. the allocator keeps moving the request to fallback shards, which then immediately preempt, causing retries and throttle spikes.
anya: logs:

2026-02-14T15:02:01Z INFO admission: admit shard=shard-42 tenant=tn-17 tokens=256
2026-02-14T15:02:01Z WARN preempt: evicting lease shard=shard-42 reason=preemptible-credit-exhausted
2026-02-14T15:02:01Z INFO fallback: rerouting req=abc123 -> shard-7
2026-02-14T15:02:01Z WARN preempt: evicting lease shard=shard-7 reason=hotspot-preemption
2026-02-14T15:02:02Z ERROR admission: throttle spike tenant=tn-17 rate=450/s

anya: small harness to repro: `go test ./orchestrator -run TestShardFallbackPreempt`
sam: can you paste the admission config used? headroom, burst credits, eviction priorities?
anya: sure — headroom=3, burst_credits=100, preemptible=true, eviction-priority: {burst: 5, preemptible: 10} (a bit aggressive).
julia: my hunch: fallback prefers any shard with capacity but ignores recent preempt history. it moves load to tiny shards that just got preempted, which then re-fallback and we oscillate.
mike: seen this pattern in previous headroom trials. solution options: (A) per-shard cooldown after preempt, (B) bias fallback toward "stable" shards, (C) small randomized delay before reassigning.
anya: per-shard cooldown seems easiest and low-risk.
sam: cooldown hurts availability if set too long. we need a way to detect true flapping vs normal churn.
julia: propose a simple detector: preempt_count_1m and reassigns_30s; mark shard as "flapping" if both exceed thresholds. then allocator treats flapping shards as last-resort.
mike: also tie cooldown to eviction type: preemptible -> short (5-15s), hotspot/oom -> longer (30-120s).
anya: should allocator also nudge the autoscaler? many fallbacks could mean capacity shortage.
sam: yes but be careful. emit a metric called fallback_amplification with counts and have scaler create a low-confidence scale intent if amplification > threshold. operator can review spikes.
julia: another mitigation: expose request hint `prefer_stable_shard=true` in SDK for job types that will retry quickly, so we avoid oscillation without changing defaults.
mike: rollout plan: implement flapping detector + per-shard cooldown behind FF, emit fallback_amplification metric, add SDK hint, canary for 48h.
anya: I'll draft a tiny RFC with thresholds, tests, and sim results.
sam: ping @orch-bot when you open the PR so CI runs the integration sim.
orch-bot: CI queued: orch-integration/sim-fallback 1724567801 -> status: queued :hourglass_flowing_sand:
anya: thanks — will post RFC link here when ready. :thumbsup:
